entry.summary: Correct permissions are the backbone of Linux security. Misconfigured bits can expose secrets, break deployments, or allow privilege escalation. This guide demystifies permission modes, shows how to set secure defaults, and offers checklists you can apply to servers, containers, and developer laptops. Permissions protect confidentiality (who can read), integrity (who can modify), and availability (who can execute).
